_comment: Observed timeline of live multi-write experiments on tomasvaron-h2sweep (Central US, Session consistency, Continuous backup), polling the account read every 5s. Companion to live_add_remove_region_timeline.json, which covers the same operations on a SINGLE-write account. Key contrast: under multi-write a joining region enters readableLocations and writableLocations in one atomic step, and enableMultipleWriteLocations itself flaps during a write-mode change.
conclusions: Continuous backup does NOT block enabling multiple write locations, despite test-resources.bicep describing them as incompatible. That comment appears to apply to account creation, not to a later PATCH.
BOTH write-mode directions are permitted: single -> multi and multi -> single each completed successfully on a normal (non-migrated) account.

enableMultipleWriteLocations FLAPS during a write-mode change, alternating true/false across successive account reads for minutes. This is a routing-mode flag, not just a list, so a client refreshing on its own cadence will alternate between multi-write and single-write routing.

Adding a region to a multi-write account puts it into readableLocations and writableLocations in a SINGLE atomic transition, with no flapping -- unlike the single-write add, which flapped for ~40s before settling.
Removing a region from a multi-write account flaps far more on the regional endpoint than the single-write case: the endpoint alternated 200 <-> 403/1008 nine times over ~5 minutes.

During that removal window writableLocations still advertises the region while its endpoint returns 403/1008. Under multi-write this is worse than under single-write, because multi-write clients route writes to their LOCAL region -- so a client colocated with the dying region retries into it, refreshes topology, is told it is still writable, and retries again.

enable_multi_write.notes: The flag reached the data plane within about a minute, then alternated true/false ~23 times over the next 5 minutes before settling on true. readableLocations/writableLocations were unaffected throughout (single-region account).

add_region_while_multi_write.notes: The new region appeared in readableLocations AND writableLocations simultaneously, in one transition, with no flapping at all. Contrast the single-write add, which flapped for ~40s. Total duration ~37 minutes, notably longer than the ~13 minute single-write add.

disable_multi_write.notes: multi -> single IS permitted here, contradicting the expectation that it is only available to migrated accounts. Flapped even more than the enable direction: ~25 alternations over ~4 minutes.

remove_region_while_multi_write.notes: The regional endpoint began failing 31s after the PATCH but then flapped 200 <-> 403/1008 nine times over ~5 minutes before DNS was withdrawn. The global account read kept advertising the region -- in BOTH readableLocations and writableLocations -- for ~6.5 minutes after the endpoint first failed.
